segments.text: Say goodbye out loud. Congratulations, you just said a blessing that's over four hundred years old.
In Shakespeare's time, people didn't say goodbye. They said God be with you. Or, the old way, God be with ye.
Say that fast enough, a few million times, and it gets squeezed. God be {wi'|wee} ye. God {b'wye.|bwye.} {Godbwye.|God-bwye.}
One of the oldest written examples is from {1573.|fifteen seventy three.} A scholar named Gabriel Harvey joked about sending a whole gallon of godbwyes.
Then God turned into good. Why? People already said good morning, good day and good night. Goodbye just fit right in.
And English isn't alone. French adieu and Spanish adiós both literally mean, to God.
So every goodbye is a tiny blessing, worn down by centuries of people in a hurry.
